title: Reservation failure isolation and soft-quota fence
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets have experienced cascading reservation failures when a subset of nodes report transient allocation errors (OOM or driver hiccups). Those failures cause aggressive decommitment, which amplifies pressure and leads to mass throttling for tenants. This PR introduces a reservation failure isolation mechanism and a soft-quota fence to reduce blast radius and preserve throughput guarantees for unaffected tenants.

Summary of changes: implement a per-reservation finality window (short TTL) that treats transient allocation errors as isolated until a small failure budget is exhausted; introduce a soft-quota fence layer that saturates capacity reduction slowly using a circuit-state (open/half-open/closed) per-tenant quota; expose configuration flags and rollout gates; add telemetry and alerts that surface isolated vs systemic reservation failures.

Design notes: the finality window keeps a reservation in a "probation" state for the first N allocation failures (configurable, default N=3) before escalating to full decommit. During probation the autoscaler will: reduce newly-admitted concurrency by a configurable fraction (default 20%), avoid immediate slot reclamation from other tenants, and start a backoff timer per-reservation. The soft-quota fence is a lightweight token-exchange implemented in the reservation allocator: when overall pool utilization is high and a tenant's circuit is open, the allocator applies a staged floor reduction (soft fence) rather than an immediate hard revoke. The fence supports rate-limited bleed-down and a fast recovery path (half-open) for healthy traffic.

API & config: new flags in the dedicated config: --reservation-probation-count, --probation-concurrency-penalty, --soft-quota-fence-enabled, --fence-bleed-rate. A new status field was added to the tenant reservation protobuf: reservation_state={HEALTHY,PROBATION,QUARANTINED}. Backwards compatibility is preserved: if the new config is disabled, behavior defaults to current immediate-decommitment flow.

Telemetry & observability: added metrics: reservation_probation_enter_total, reservation_probation_exit_total, reservation_quarantine_total, soft_fence_bleed_bytes, tenant_fence_state_count{state}. Dashboards: a dedicated panel that separates isolated probation events from system-wide failures; alerts: >5% of reservations quarantined for >10m triggers P1.

Testing & rollout: unit tests for allocator state machine and quota fence transitions; integration tests that simulate transient allocation failures and assert throughput delta <5% for unaffected tenants; a canary rollout plan that enables probation only for 10% of pods, followed by 50% and global if no regression. The PR also includes a smoke test harness for failure-injection.

Deployment considerations: default configuration is conservative; operators can tune probation count and bleed rate for their fleet profile. The rollout plan recommends enabling telemetry first and verifying alert thresholds before widening the gate.

Related: references ENG-2426 for incident context and ENG-2489 for tenant SLA requirements.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc linked and reviewed
- [x] unit + integration tests added
- [x] telemetry and dashboards updated
- [x] canary rollout plan documented

Notes: this PR intentionally avoids changing long-term reservation accounting; it focuses on transient failure isolation and graceful degradation to keep the majority of tenants unaffected during short-lived node faults.
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial allocator state-machine and probation logic; soft-quota fence token path; telemetry and tests; docs + canary rollout notes
ci_checks: benchmarks: no regression in P50 latency (<2%), throughput change <3%
review_conversation: Evan Chu: Nice approach — can you clarify why we prefer a probation counter over exponential backoff?

Priya Shah: The probation counter keeps the failure handling bounded and makes it easier to reason about SLA windows. We add a backoff timer separately for admission; both are combined in the probation state.
Miguel Torres: Please add a metric for probation-age distribution so SREs can detect long-tail stuck reservations.
Priya Shah: Added reservation_probation_age_seconds histogram in the last commit.
Janelle Park: Integration tests look flakey on my run; I saw a timing race in the harness. Can we make the harness write deterministic logs?
Priya Shah: Fixed harness race by switching to mocked clock in integration tests; re-ran CI.
Miguel Torres: Approve after nit on config naming (probation -> probation_count) addressed.
Evan Chu: Approved. Recommend squash merge; leave detailed changelog entry in release notes.
release_notes: Introduce reservation failure probation window and a soft-quota fence to reduce blast radius from transient allocation errors. Adds new config flags and telemetry. Default behavior is conservative; see docs for tuning guidance.
notes_for_ops: Enable telemetry panels and watch reservation_quarantine_total closely during canary. Start with --reservation-probation-count=3 and --fence-bleed-rate=0.05 per-minute. If tenant throughput degrades, reduce penalty or widen probation count.
postmerge_tasks: Schedule a follow-up to evaluate 24h telemetry and adjust default bleed rate; add an automated mitigation runbook to the SRE playbook.
why_unique: This PR focuses on isolating transient reservation allocation failures with a probation state and a soft fence bleed-down — a different failure-handling model than immediate decommitment or global throttling used previously. It emphasizes telemetry-first rollout and a conservative default configuration.
